Per document, not per story: the clause says "a stored document". All stories of a document compose under one token, new stories included. The MT expected_outputs say "stored story"; the spec wins.

Bounds, all Studio values: token 1024 bytes of printable ASCII, 64 upgrades per record, 4096 stories per upgrade, wire form 1 MiB. Over a bound: BudgetExceeded for counts and input, InvalidField for a token. An upgrade target past the limit answers composition_token_unknown, since it can be no known token.

Diffable (Studio reading, the clause and the session define no diff): from-token, to-token and the stories it affects, in Applied::composition_upgrade and in the record, so it survives a reopen. The session does not compose, so no glyph-level comparison is built. The undo diff is the upgrade reversed; only the upgrade is added to the record, undo removes it.

Stories it affects: Payload::Text story ids of the document plus stories[].story_id of the text entry, sorted, unique: every story could recompose differently, so this is the set at risk, not a computed set that did change. The session reads that one field of a host-owned entry through Folio. A text entry that does not read refuses the upgrade folio_rejected: no shorter diff is recorded.

Undo and redo are CompositionTokenChange::Restore, accepted only as the removal or re-adding of one recorded upgrade. A restore to an older token with no record of the move is composition_token_older, a newer one composition_token_unrecorded. Redo restores the recorded story list, not a fresh one.
The same token again is no change, no revision, no entry created. An upgrade over a repeated or unparsable entry is value_conflict, over a later build's token composition_token_unknown.

Direct set_composition_token_record / set_document_entry stays possible, as for the sequence entries: it validates, refuses an unknown token, is not a revision and can remove an entry or replace an unknown token. It is an explicit host action and can move a document to an older token unrecorded; the recorded operation is submit_composition_token. Flagged for the validator.
A commit authority receives the successor document and the step travels in the binding hash, as multicam and the sequence records.
Imports are new documents and record the current token, so an imported story with U+2028 composes under @3.

Code composition_token_refused is reported when the current token shapes a story the document token refuses; found by shaping again under the current token, on the report path only, for failed stories only. A failure under every token gets no composition cause.
